zh.summary: 將「更有效率」拆成可觀察指標，標明假設與資料來源，讓需求變更、測試證據和下一步決定可以相互追溯。
objectives: 為功能結果與使用者任務各定義可觀察的成功條件。
為指標寫出分母、量測方法、基準與適用範圍。
將假設、需求候選、確認決定及修訂理由接回 problem.md。

readingGuide.goal: 為功能結果與使用者任務各定義可觀察的成功條件。
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md、文字編輯器與本章合成算例；不收集真人成績或計時。
readingGuide.route: 先看情境與原理，再比較例子，最後擴寫 problem.md 並用檢核題自查。
readingGuide.output: problem.md 有可重做的指標定義、假設、需求候選與變更紀錄，結果欄如實保留未測量。

sections.heading: 如何判定系統真的有用？
paragraphs: 這堂課最重要的觀念是：做出一個功能，不代表解決了一個問題；而且，即使問題看起來改善了，也不代表一定是你的系統造成的。
我們必須學會三件事情：

1. 定義成功（Success Criteria）：怎樣的結果才算真正成功？
2. 驗證假設（Hypothesis Testing）：我們相信某個設計有用，有沒有證據支持？
3. 保留需求紀錄（Requirements Traceability）：為什麼當初要這樣設計？後來為什麼修改？結果有沒有通過驗證？
這些能力不只適用於軟體工程，也適用於醫療、金融、教育、製造、政府行政、科學研究，甚至企業管理。
本課以跨產業例子說明成功指標、假設與需求紀錄，以及實務上的驗證方法。

sections.heading: 一、先理解整堂課的核心：我們怎麼知道一件事情真的改善了？
paragraphs: 假設有一家醫院，病人從報到到看診，平均需要等待 50 分鐘。
院長希望改善這個問題，於是資訊部門開發了一套 AI 智慧掛號與分流系統。
三個月後，資訊部門向院長報告：
「我們完成了 15 個功能、導入了 AI、自動化了掛號作業，而且系統可以在兩秒內處理一筆資料。」
院長可能會回答：
「很好，但病人現在還是要等 50 分鐘嗎？」
這就是本堂課的起點。
系統處理速度變快，不代表病人等待時間就會縮短。真正的瓶頸也許是醫師人力不足，或檢查室排程不合理。
因此，我們必須區分：

- 產出（Output）：我們做出了什麼？例如完成 AI 掛號功能。
- 結果（Outcome）：使用者的情況有沒有改善？例如平均候診時間縮短。
- 影響（Impact）：長期而言，這項改善帶來什麼價值？例如減少延誤、改善醫療服務品質。

blocks.caption: 圖 1｜從問題到決策的六個環節
blocks.description: 箭頭表示判斷的閱讀順序，不保證改善或因果成立。這個流程可以反覆循環；如果證據不支持假設，就需要回頭修正，而不是勉強宣布成功。

items.title: 1. Problem｜問題
items.body: 病人等待時間過長

items.title: 2. Requirement｜需求
items.body: 系統要能依報到狀態與看診規則安排候診流程

items.title: 3. Hypothesis｜假設
items.body: 減少人工排程時間，可能縮短病人等待時間

items.title: 4. Metric｜成功指標
items.body: 候診時間、準時看診率、排程錯誤率

items.title: 5. Evidence｜證據
items.body: 系統測試、前後比較、實際操作紀錄

items.title: 6. Decision｜決策
items.body: 通過驗收、修改設計，或重新檢查問題

paragraphs: 注意：需求是「系統應該做到什麼」；假設是「為什麼這麼做可能有效」；指標是「我們打算怎麼判定效果」。這三者不能混為一談。

sections.heading: 二、功能成功與使用者成功，是兩件不同的事
paragraphs: 我們先認識兩個非常重要的詞。
Functional Metric（功能指標），指的是系統是否按照規定正確運作。
Task Metric（任務指標），指的是使用者是否真的能完成原本要做的事情。
例如，一家銀行導入 AI 文件辨識系統。
工程師說：「我們的文件辨識 API 可以正常回傳資料，而且 99% 的請求都沒有發生系統錯誤。」
這是功能方面的好消息。
但銀行的徵信人員可能說：「我還是需要花很長的時間修正辨識結果，而且現在多了一道檢查步驟。」
也就是說，系統正常運作，卻不一定提高工作效率。
我們再比較幾個不同產業。

blocks.caption: 表 1
headers: 功能指標：系統做得對嗎？
任務指標：人真的受益嗎？
rows: AI 是否正確讀取病歷欄位
醫護能否更快完成正確紀錄
配送演算法是否成功產生路線
AI 是否成功產生練習題
學生是否真正學會解題
瑕疵檢測是否正確辨識缺陷
能否減少不良品流出，又不過度誤擋良品
系統是否正確檢查申請文件
民眾能否自行完成申請

paragraphs: 因此，不能只測試程式有沒有出錯，還要看人能不能完成工作。
而且，最好再加入第三種觀察角度：Guardrail Metric（護欄指標）。
它的意思是，改善一件事情時，不可以讓另一件重要的事情變得更糟。
例如：
一家物流公司希望提高配送速度，但不能因此增加交通事故；一家醫院希望減少候診時間，但不能因此提高病歷或分流錯誤。

blocks.caption: 圖 2｜功能、任務與護欄
blocks.description: 這是三種平行的觀察角度，沒有先後或因果關係。

items.title: 功能
items.body: 有沒有做對？

items.title: 任務
items.body: 有沒有幫助？

items.title: 護欄
items.body: 有沒有副作用？

paragraphs: 這三種角度共同回答：系統是否值得採用？

sections.heading: 三、成功指標要怎麼計算？最重要的是分母
paragraphs: 很多人會說：「我們的系統有 90% 的成功率。」
但這句話其實沒有想像中那麼有意義。
我們應該追問：「90% 是從哪些案例計算出來的？什麼叫成功？有沒有排除失敗的案例？」

blocks.heading: 例子：工廠的瑕疵檢測系統
paragraphs: 假設工廠正在試驗一套 AI 檢測設備。
我們準備六件測試產品，其中四件確實有瑕疵，另外兩件是良品。
如果問題是「有瑕疵的產品，有多少比例被成功阻擋？」
那麼公式就是：
瑕疵阻擋率＝成功阻擋的瑕疵品／全部瑕疵品。
請注意，分母是四件瑕疵品，不是全部六件產品。

blocks.heading: 自己動手實驗
paragraphs: 試著調整下面兩個數字，看看系統的表現如何變化。

blocks.caption: 圖 3｜瑕疵阻擋與良品放行
blocks.description: 固定四件瑕疵品、兩件良品。數據為教學用的合成案例，不是真實工廠測試紀錄；下載圖保留預設3／4與0／2，不隨操作改變。

items.title: 有瑕疵的 4 件產品，成功阻擋幾件？
正常的 2 件產品，被錯誤阻擋幾件？

sections.heading: 分母、錯誤代價與小樣本界線
paragraphs: 這個例子其實引出了機器學習當中很重要的觀念：

- False Negative（偽陰性，漏判）：真的有問題，系統卻沒有發現。
- False Positive（偽陽性，誤判）：原本沒有問題，系統卻誤認為有問題。
如果是醫療檢查，漏判可能意味著沒有發現疾病；如果是銀行反詐騙，誤判可能意味著正常交易被阻擋。
不同產業的錯誤代價不同，因此成功指標及驗收標準也不應該完全相同。
另外有兩個容易出錯的地方。
首先，假設根本沒有任何瑕疵測試案例，分母就是零。這時不能把阻擋率寫成 100%，應該寫「未測得」，因為根本沒有驗證到這種情況。
其次，四件瑕疵品都成功阻擋，只能說這四件測試案例全部通過，不能直接推論整個系統的真實準確率必定為 100%。
小樣本通過驗收，與證明整體可靠性，是不同層次的主張。

sections.heading: 四、為什麼系統變快了，不代表它真的提高效率？
paragraphs: 這是本章非常值得深入理解的部分。
假設一家律師事務所想使用 AI 協助整理案件資料。
原本律師需要 30 分鐘整理一份文件，使用 AI 後，系統只需要 5 分鐘就能生成摘要。
於是軟體公司宣稱：「工作效率提高六倍。」
但是我們繼續觀察，發現律師還需要花 20 分鐘確認 AI 摘要是否正確。
實際上：
這是示意數字。真正節省的工作時間只有 5 分鐘，約 16.7%，不是六倍的整體效率。
更重要的是，我們還不知道 AI 是否增加了錯誤風險。

blocks.heading: 這時要認識 Baseline（基準值）
paragraphs: Baseline 就是改善之前的狀況。
例如，原本平均要 30 分鐘，這個 30 分鐘就可以作為比較基準。但必須確定兩邊測量的是相同工作。
英國政府的數位服務績效指南也強調，指標要連結服務目的、建立基準值、確認資料來源，並結合使用者研究，而不是只有漂亮的績效數字。
實務上，我們要注意三個問題。
第一，起點與終點必須一致。
舊方式從收到文件開始算，新方式卻從文件已經整理完畢才開始計時，這不是公平比較。
第二，完成品質必須一致。
舊流程做出正確文件，新流程雖然比較快，卻有三處重要錯誤，不能直接當成效率改善。
第三，必須排除其他可能原因。
例如，律師第二次整理相同案件，原本就比較熟悉資料，自然會更快。
這叫做 Practice Effect（練習效應）。
如果要嚴謹比較，可以讓不同參與者交換使用新舊系統的順序，並使用難度相近的任務。這種設計稱為 Counterbalancing（平衡順序設計）。
還要記錄沒有完成工作的人。如果十個人只有五個人成功，就不能只計算這五個成功者的速度，完全不提其餘五人的失敗。

sections.heading: 五、Hypothesis：假設不是事實，而是等待驗證的想法
paragraphs: 很多系統設計錯誤，不是工程師不會寫程式，而是大家一開始相信了一個沒有驗證過的想法。
例如，一所大學發現學生在數學課的成績不佳。
校方提出：「我們應該開發 AI 家教系統，讓學生隨時提問。」
這是一個可能合理的方案，但並不表示 AI 家教一定能改善學習。
學生的問題也許是缺乏先備知識、練習不足，或不理解教材使用的符號。
因此，我們應該寫出可以驗證的假設。

blocks.caption: 圖 4｜假設 H-01：AI 家教是否有助於學習？
blocks.description: 四欄共同定義待驗假設；示範門檻需在研究前具體約定，這裡沒有學習成效的實測結果。

items.title: 假設內容
items.body: 提供能逐步提示、而非直接公布答案的 AI 家教，可能提高學生獨立解決新題目的能力。

items.title: 測量方式
items.body: 使用難度相近但未見過的題目，測量學生在沒有 AI 幫助下的解題能力。

items.title: 示範成功門檻
items.body: 實驗組在事先定義的測驗指標上優於適當的對照組，且效果達到預定的教育實務重要程度。

items.title: 可能反證
items.body: 學生使用 AI 時表現變好，卻無法獨立解決新的題目。

paragraphs: 這裡最重要的是「反證」。
你不只是問：「有什麼證據支持我的設計？」
你還要問：「出現什麼結果時，我應該承認這個設計可能沒有達到目標？」
這就是 Falsifiability（可反駁性）在工程實務中的精神。
不過，假設沒有獲得支持，不一定代表它已經被徹底推翻。也可能是樣本太少、測量不敏感，或實驗設計存在問題。因此應綜合證據品質、效果大小與不確定性判斷。

sections.heading: 六、需求紀錄為什麼重要？因為半年後沒有人記得當初為什麼這麼設計
paragraphs: 我們換到金融業來看。
假設銀行開發一套 AI 徵信報告系統。
最早的需求是：
「使用者可以上傳資料，經過檢查後，產生報告。」
工程師完成之後，測試人員發現一個問題：

blocks.caption: 圖 5｜修改後沿用舊狀態的風險
blocks.description: 編號表示合成案例的時間順序。資料 B 必須重新檢查，不能沿用資料 A 的結果；本圖沒有宣稱真實銀行曾發生此事件。

items.title: 步驟 1｜檢查資料 A
items.body: 系統顯示資料 A 通過檢查。

items.title: 步驟 2｜使用者修改資料
items.body: 使用者把資料 A 改成 B，並更改了重要的金額欄位。

items.title: 步驟 3｜系統仍然顯示通過
items.body: 系統沿用了資料 A 的檢查結果，沒有重新驗證 B。

items.title: 步驟 4｜使用者匯出報告
items.body: 未重新檢查的資料 B 被匯出，形成風險。

paragraphs: 因此工程師增加了一條新規則：
「只要會影響檢查結果的資料被修改，先前的通過狀態就必須失效，重新檢查後才能匯出。」
但如果工程師只是直接修改程式，沒有記錄原因，未來接手的人可能會問：
「為什麼每次修改一個欄位，都必須重新檢查？能不能把它移除來提升效能？」
他可能不知道，這條規則其實是為了避免輸出未經驗證的金融資料。
這就需要 Requirements Traceability（需求可追溯性）。
它的本質是：
讓每一個重要決定，都能追查它源自哪個問題、由誰確認、為什麼改變，以及如何證明它已經實現。
例如：

blocks.caption: 表 4
rows: 重要資料修改後必須重新檢查
自動使舊狀態失效，可降低未經檢查匯出的風險
指定的過期狀態測試案例必須全部阻擋
修改金額、姓名等影響檢查結果的欄位後測試
新增檢查結果失效機制
待執行測試，尚未取得結果

paragraphs: 這些代號只是方便管理的示範，並不是唯一的正式標準。
實際上還應記錄來源、提出者、確認角色、日期、版本、決策理由以及狀態。這能避免把尚未確認的建議，誤當成已核准需求。

sections.heading: 七、Verification、Validation、Evaluation 有什麼不同？
paragraphs: 這三個英文詞在 AI 與軟體工程中很容易混淆。

blocks.caption: 表 5
rows: 做的是使用者真正需要的嗎？
系統能否解決實際問題？
透過什麼指標衡量表現？

paragraphs: 例如，一家餐廳開發自助點餐系統。
Verification 是檢查「按下送出訂單，廚房是否收到正確餐點與數量」。
Validation 是檢查「客人能否順利完成點餐，而且這個系統是否真的改善服務問題」。
Evaluation 則是測量「點餐平均花多少時間、訂錯率多少、完成率多少」。
它們不是彼此取代，而是互相補充。

sections.heading: 八、實務上怎麼開始？用一份 problem.md 就足夠
paragraphs: M03-05 很重要的一個精神，是不要為了管理需求而先導入過度複雜的工具。
小型專案可以先從 Markdown 文件開始。
下面用「物流配送異常通知系統」示範。

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: 合成範例；基準、結果與決策狀態依原稿保留。
blocks.code:
# 專案：物流配送異常通知

## Problem｜問題
顧客無法及時知道配送異常，
導致反覆查詢客服。

## Requirement｜需求
R-01：配送異常發生後，
系統應發送明確的異常通知。

狀態：需求候選，待業務確認。

## Hypothesis｜假設
H-01：主動通知異常及處理方式，
可以降低顧客重複查詢。

狀態：尚未驗證。

## Metric｜成功指標
M-01：通知成功送達率
公式：成功送達數 / 應通知事件數

M-02：重複查詢率
公式：指定期間內重複查詢的異常訂單數
      / 同期間符合條件的異常訂單數

M-03：異常處理完成時間
起點：異常首次被記錄
終點：異常處理完成且狀態確認

上述指標均需確認適用範圍、
資料來源、測量期間與成功門檻。

## Evidence｜證據
基準值：未測量
新系統結果：未測量
測試紀錄：尚未取得

## Change Log｜變更紀錄
C-01：待確認是否新增通知重試機制
原因：通知可能無法成功送達
決策者：待確認
日期：待確認
狀態：提案中

paragraphs: 這份文件有兩個關鍵價值。
第一，它把問題、需求、假設、指標與證據接在一起，避免只記錄功能清單。
第二，它明確區分「我們打算做到」與「我們已經證明做到」。
尤其要注意，不能因為 AI 已經產生測試計畫，就把測試結果寫成通過。
AI 可以協助撰寫需求、設計測試案例、整理執行紀錄，但它沒有實際觀察到的結果，就不應宣稱驗收完成。

sections.heading: 九、將這堂課轉換成真正可執行的工作方法
paragraphs: 當你下一次要設計一個 AI 系統，不論是醫療、教育、研究或企業服務，都可以先完成以下五項工作。

blocks.caption: 表 6
rows: 系統必須做到哪些事情？
為什麼相信這個設計有用？
指標、分母、基準、門檻、資料來源
測試證據、驗收決策、變更紀錄

paragraphs: 這份架構也與 英國 GOV.UK 的服務績效指標設計指南（本課下方來源連結） 一致：先理解服務目的，再提出假設、決定如何測量、找到資料來源，最後根據結果持續修正。
在需要進行正式驗收的專案，還應為重要指標預先設定通過條件，並考慮樣本代表性、風險、成本及測量的不確定性。

sections.heading: 十、理解檢核：你能不能辨識不可靠的成功宣稱？
paragraphs: 依下列合成案例檢查主張與證據。

blocks.caption: 圖 6｜整合案例：一家製造公司導入 AI 品質檢測系統
blocks.description: 上述數字全部是假設資料，沒有提供實驗安排、樣本代表性或計時範圍。

items.title: 公司提出三個主張
items.body:
「AI 已經成功上線。」

「瑕疵檢測效果很好。」

「工廠整體生產效率提高 30%。」

items.title: 人工舊流程
items.body: 平均 10 分鐘

items.title: AI 新流程
items.body: 平均 7 分鐘

paragraphs: 請回答：

1. 指標計算：這套 AI 的瑕疵阻擋率是多少？良品正確放行率是多少？兩個指標分別告訴我們什麼？
2. 證據判斷：10 分鐘變成 7 分鐘，是否足以證明生產效率提高 30%？還缺少哪些資訊？
3. 假設驗證：如果管理層相信「AI 可以降低品質檢查成本」，你會如何把這句話轉換成可驗證的假設？
4. 需求追溯：如果後續發現機器重新校正後，先前的合格判斷可能已經不適用，你會增加什麼需求，又該留下哪些紀錄？
5. 整體決策：假設你是這間工廠的專案負責人，根據現有證據，你會決定直接全面上線、繼續限制範圍試驗，還是停止計畫？為什麼？
請先嘗試回答，再展開參考解析，逐項檢查推理與計算。
最後記住這堂課最重要的一句話：好的工程，不只是把東西做出來，而是能清楚說明為什麼要做、如何判斷成功，以及有什麼證據支持我們的決定。

exercise.environment: problem.md、文字編輯器與本章合成算例；不收集真人成績或計時。
steps: 選一項功能指標與一項任務指標，各寫分母、起終點、資料來源與未測量欄位。
用四筆缺漏、三筆阻擋的合成卡計算，再解釋為何完整案例不進該分母；另處理分母為零。
新增 H-01、R-01 與一筆變更，保留來源、確認角色與理由，請同儕指出下一個仍待驗證的主張。
exercise.expected: problem.md 有可重做的指標定義、假設、需求候選與變更紀錄，結果欄如實保留未測量。
exercise.check: 能算出 3／4＝75% 並判定本版缺漏阻擋要求未通過；不把合成算例當真人或實際軟體結果。
exercise.cleanup: 保留合成標記與原始定義，不公開真人任務記錄；未測量項目保持未測量。

openChecks.prompt: 指標計算：這套 AI 的瑕疵阻擋率是多少？良品正確放行率是多少？兩個指標分別告訴我們什麼？
answer: 瑕疵阻擋率＝18／20＝90%；良品正確放行率＝(80－12)／80＝85%。前者看漏擋，後者看誤擋；不能只報其中一個來宣稱整體效果良好。

openChecks.prompt: 證據判斷：10 分鐘變成 7 分鐘，是否足以證明生產效率提高 30%？還缺少哪些資訊？
answer: 10變7分鐘是示範工作時間減少30%，不足以證明工廠整體生產效率提高30%。還要固定任務、難度、起終點、產出品質與檢查修正時間，記錄失敗、放棄、樣本與其他變因。固定工時產出量與每件耗時的百分比也不同；沒有這些資料就無法推論工廠層級成效。

openChecks.prompt: 假設驗證：如果管理層相信「AI 可以降低品質檢查成本」，你會如何把這句話轉換成可驗證的假設？
answer: 例如：在事先界定的產品與期間內，AI輔助檢查可降低每件合格產出的總檢查成本，並維持漏擋與誤擋在預定護欄內。先定基準、成本範圍、對照方式、樣本與門檻；納入設備、人工覆核、重工與錯誤成本。若成本不降或品質護欄變差，假設未獲支持。

openChecks.prompt: 需求追溯：如果後續發現機器重新校正後，先前的合格判斷可能已經不適用，你會增加什麼需求，又該留下哪些紀錄？
answer: 增加重新校正後使受影響的舊合格結果失效、重新檢查才可放行的需求。保留校正版本、受影響資料範圍、R/H/M/T/C/E連結、來源、確認角色、日期、理由與狀態；先寫待驗，實際執行後再附證據與決策。

openChecks.prompt: 整體決策：假設你是這間工廠的專案負責人，根據現有證據，你會決定直接全面上線、繼續限制範圍試驗，還是停止計畫？為什麼？
answer: 現有資料不足以支持全面上線；可在風險可控制且有明確護欄、停止條件與證據計畫時繼續限制範圍試驗。若無法控制風險或成本則停止或延後。說明選擇依據、待補資料與下一個決策門檻，不能把合成紀錄當成真實試驗已完成。

en.summary: Turn “more efficient” into observable measures, label assumptions and data sources, and connect requirement changes with test evidence and subsequent decisions.
objectives: Define observable success conditions for both program behavior and user tasks.
Specify denominators, measurement methods, baselines and scope for metrics.
Bring assumptions, proposed requirements, confirmed decisions and revision reasons back to problem.md.

readingGuide.goal: Define observable success conditions for both program behavior and user tasks.
readingGuide.startingPoint: problem.md, a text editor and this lesson’s synthetic arithmetic. Do not collect actual participant scores or timing.
readingGuide.route: Read the scenario and principles, compare examples, then expand problem.md and use the checks to review your understanding.
readingGuide.output: Reproducible metric definitions, assumptions, proposed requirements and change records in problem.md, with results honestly left unmeasured.

sections.heading: How do we determine whether a system helps?
paragraphs: Building a feature does not establish that a problem has been solved. Even when a problem appears to improve, the improvement may have causes other than your system.
We need three abilities:

1. Define success criteria: what result would count as success?
2. Test hypotheses: what evidence supports our belief that a design helps?
3. Maintain requirements traceability: why was a design chosen, why was it changed, and has the result passed verification?
These abilities apply to software engineering, healthcare, finance, education, manufacturing, public administration, scientific research and business management.
This lesson uses examples across industries to explain success criteria, hypotheses, requirements records and practical verification methods.

sections.heading: 1. How do we know whether something has improved?
paragraphs: Suppose patients at a hospital wait an average of 50 minutes between checking in and seeing a clinician.
The director wants to address this problem, so the IT department develops an AI registration and patient-routing system.
Three months later, the department reports:
“We completed 15 features, introduced AI, automated registration, and can process one record in two seconds.”
The director might reply:
“Good, but do patients still wait 50 minutes?”
That question is our starting point.
Faster system processing does not necessarily shorten patients’ waiting time. The actual bottleneck might be insufficient clinical staff or poor scheduling of examination rooms.
We therefore distinguish:

- Output: what did we build? For example, an AI registration feature.
- Outcome: did users’ circumstances improve? For example, shorter average waiting time.
- Impact: what value does that improvement create over time? For example, fewer delays and better healthcare service quality.

blocks.caption: Figure 1 | Six links from problem to decision
blocks.description: Arrows show the order of reasoning, not demonstrated improvement or causation. Repeat the cycle when needed: if evidence does not support the hypothesis, revise it rather than declaring success.

items.title: 1. Problem
items.body: Patients wait too long

items.title: 2. Requirement
items.body: Arrange the waiting workflow using check-in status and clinical scheduling rules

items.title: 3. Hypothesis
items.body: Reducing manual scheduling time may shorten patient waiting time

items.title: 4. Metric
items.body: Waiting time, on-time consultation rate and scheduling error rate

items.title: 5. Evidence
items.body: System tests, before-and-after comparisons and actual operation records

items.title: 6. Decision
items.body: Accept, revise the design, or re-examine the problem

paragraphs: A requirement states what the system should do; a hypothesis explains why doing it might help; a metric specifies how we intend to judge the effect. These are distinct concepts.

sections.heading: 2. Functional success and user success are different questions
paragraphs: Start with two terms.
A functional metric asks whether the system operates correctly according to its requirements.
A task metric asks whether users can actually accomplish the work they set out to do.
For example, a bank introduces AI document recognition.
An engineer says: “Our recognition API returns data normally, and 99% of requests produce no system error.”
That is good news about functionality.
But a credit analyst might say: “I still spend a long time correcting recognition results, and now I have another checking step.”
A normally operating system does not necessarily improve work efficiency.
Compare several industries:

blocks.caption: Table 1
headers: Functional metric: does the system operate correctly?
Task metric: does it help people?
rows: Does AI read medical-record fields correctly?
Can staff complete correct records faster?
Does the routing algorithm generate routes successfully?
Does AI generate practice questions successfully?
Do students actually learn to solve problems?
Does defect detection identify defects correctly?
Can it reduce defective shipments without blocking too many good products?
Does the system check application documents correctly?

paragraphs: Test both whether the program operates without errors and whether people can complete their work.
A third perspective is the guardrail metric.
A guardrail checks that improving one thing does not make another important thing worse.
For example:
A logistics company wants faster deliveries without more traffic accidents. A hospital wants shorter waits without more medical-record or patient-routing errors.

blocks.caption: Figure 2 | Function, task and guardrails
blocks.description: These are parallel perspectives, not a sequence or a causal chain.

items.title: Function
items.body: Does it work correctly?

items.title: Task
items.body: Does it help?

items.title: Guardrail
items.body: Does it cause side effects?

paragraphs: Together, these perspectives help answer whether the system is worth adopting.

sections.heading: 3. How do we calculate success? Start with the denominator
paragraphs: People often say: “Our system has a 90% success rate.”
That statement is less informative than it appears.
Ask: “Which cases produced that 90%? What counts as success? Were failures excluded?”

blocks.heading: Example: defect detection in a factory
paragraphs: Suppose a factory is trying an AI inspection device.
We prepare six test products: four genuinely defective products and two good products.
If the question is “What proportion of defective products were successfully blocked?”
The formula is:
Defect blocking rate = successfully blocked defective products / all defective products.
The denominator is the four defective products, not all six products.

blocks.heading: Try the calculation
paragraphs: Adjust the two counts below and observe how the reported performance changes.

blocks.caption: Figure 3 | Blocking defects and releasing good products
blocks.description: The example fixes four defective products and two good products. These are synthetic teaching data, not a real factory test. The download retains the default 3/4 and 0/2 counts rather than changing with the controls.

items.title: Of 4 defective products, how many are blocked?
Of 2 good products, how many are incorrectly blocked?
Correct release rate for good products

sections.heading: Denominators, error costs and small-sample limits
paragraphs: This example introduces two important machine-learning concepts:

- False negative: a real problem exists, but the system fails to detect it.
- False positive: no problem exists, but the system incorrectly reports one.
In medical screening, a false negative can mean a disease goes undetected. In bank fraud detection, a false positive can mean a legitimate transaction is blocked.
The costs of errors differ across industries, so success metrics and acceptance criteria should reflect those differences.
Two other mistakes deserve attention.
First, if there are no defective test cases, the denominator is zero. Do not report a 100% blocking rate. Report “not measured”: this situation has not been tested.
Second, blocking all four defective products establishes that those four cases passed. It does not establish that the system’s true overall accuracy is necessarily 100%.
Passing acceptance checks on a small sample and demonstrating overall reliability support different levels of claim.

sections.heading: 4. Why does faster processing not necessarily mean more efficient work?
paragraphs: Consider the entire workflow.
Suppose a law firm wants AI to help organize case materials.
A lawyer previously spent 30 minutes organizing one document. With AI, the system generates a summary in just 5 minutes.
The software company claims: “Work efficiency has increased sixfold.”
Further observation shows that the lawyer also needs 20 minutes to verify the AI summary.
The comparison is:

blocks.caption: Table 3
rows: Organizing material and producing the summary

paragraphs: These are illustrative numbers. The actual time saving is only 5 minutes, about 16.7%; they do not show a sixfold improvement in overall efficiency.
We also do not yet know whether AI increases the risk of errors.

blocks.heading: What is a baseline?
paragraphs: A baseline describes the situation before an improvement.
For example, the previous average of 30 minutes can provide a baseline, provided both measurements cover the same work.
The UK government’s service performance guidance connects metrics to service purpose, baseline performance and data sources, and combines measurement with user research.
In practice, check three things.
First, use the same start and end points.
It is not a fair comparison if the old workflow is timed from receipt of the document but timing for the new workflow begins only after the material has already been organized.
Second, require the same completion quality.
If the old workflow produces a correct document while the faster new workflow leaves three important errors, speed alone does not establish improved efficiency.
Third, investigate other possible causes.
For example, lawyers may work faster the second time they organize the same case because they already know the material.
This is a practice effect.
For a more rigorous comparison, vary the order in which participants use the old and new systems, using tasks of comparable difficulty. This is called counterbalancing.
Also record people who do not complete the work. If only five out of ten people succeed, do not report only the five successful participants’ times while omitting the other five failures.

sections.heading: 5. A hypothesis is an idea awaiting evidence
paragraphs: Many design failures begin with an untested belief rather than an inability to write software.
For example, a university finds that students are doing poorly in mathematics.
The university proposes: “We should develop an AI tutor so students can ask questions at any time.”
That may be a reasonable option, but it does not establish that an AI tutor will improve learning.
Students might lack prerequisite knowledge or practice, or misunderstand the notation used in the course.
Write a testable hypothesis.

blocks.caption: Figure 4 | Hypothesis H-01: does an AI tutor help learning?
blocks.description: The four fields define a hypothesis awaiting evidence. Specify the illustrative threshold before the study; no measured learning result is reported here.

items.title: Hypothesis
items.body: An AI tutor that provides progressive hints rather than directly revealing answers may improve students’ ability to solve new problems independently.

items.title: Measurement
items.body: Use previously unseen questions of comparable difficulty to measure problem-solving without AI assistance.

items.title: Illustrative success threshold
items.body: The intervention group outperforms an appropriate control group on a predefined test metric, with an effect reaching the agreed level of educational practical importance.

items.title: Possible counterevidence
items.body: Students perform better with AI but cannot independently solve new problems.

paragraphs: The possible counterevidence matters.
Ask: “What evidence would support this design?”
Also ask: “What result should make us acknowledge that the design may not have achieved its goal?”
This is the spirit of falsifiability in engineering practice.

However, a hypothesis that receives no support has not necessarily been conclusively refuted. The sample might be too small, the measurement too insensitive, or the study design flawed. Judge evidence quality, effect size and uncertainty together.

sections.heading: 6. Why keep requirements records? Six months later, the rationale may be forgotten
paragraphs: Consider a financial example.
Suppose a bank develops an AI credit-report system.
The original requirement is:
“Users can upload data, have it checked, and generate a report.”
After implementation, a tester discovers a problem:

blocks.caption: Figure 5 | The risk of reusing status after edits
blocks.description: Numbers show the chronology of a synthetic example. Data B must be checked again; data A’s result cannot be reused. This is not a report of an incident at a real bank.

items.title: Step 1 | Check data A
items.body: The system shows that data A passed.

items.title: Step 2 | The user edits the data
items.body: The user changes data A into B, including important amount fields.

items.title: Step 3 | The system still shows a pass
items.body: The system reuses data A’s result without checking B.

items.title: Step 4 | The user exports a report
items.body: Unchecked data B is exported, creating risk.

paragraphs: The engineer therefore adds a rule:
“Whenever data that affects the check is modified, the previous pass status must become invalid. Export is allowed only after a new check.”
If the engineer changes the program without recording why, a future maintainer may ask:
“Why must we check again whenever a field is edited? Could we remove this to improve performance?”
The maintainer may not know that the rule prevents unchecked financial data from being exported.
This is why we need requirements traceability.
Its purpose is:
For each important decision, we should be able to trace the originating problem, who confirmed it, why it changed, and how its implementation can be demonstrated.
For example:

blocks.caption: Table 4
rows: Recheck after important data is modified
Automatically invalidating old status may reduce the risk of unchecked exports
Every specified stale-status test case must be blocked
Test after editing amount, name or other fields that affect the check
Add a mechanism to invalidate check results
Tests pending; no result obtained yet

paragraphs: These identifiers are illustrative management aids, not a unique formal standard.
Also record the source, proposer, confirming role, date, version, decision rationale and status. This helps prevent an unconfirmed suggestion from being treated as an approved requirement.

sections.heading: 7. How do verification, validation and evaluation differ?
paragraphs: These terms are easily confused in AI and software engineering.

blocks.caption: Table 5
rows: Did we implement it according to specification?
Does the system meet its requirements?
Did we build what users actually need?
Can the system address the real problem?
What metrics are used to measure performance?

paragraphs: For example, a restaurant develops a self-service ordering system.
Verification checks whether submitting an order sends the correct dishes and quantities to the kitchen.
Validation checks whether customers can complete their orders smoothly and whether the system actually improves the service problem.
Evaluation measures ordering time, order error rate and completion rate.
These activities complement one another.

sections.heading: 8. Start with a problem.md file
paragraphs: A useful principle of M03-05 is to avoid introducing overly complex tools before you need them to manage requirements.
A small project can begin with Markdown.
Here is a delivery-exception notification example. The original Chinese problem.md is retained verbatim in both languages.

blocks.heading: problem.md
paragraphs: Synthetic example; baseline, results and decision status are retained as supplied.
blocks.code:
# 專案：物流配送異常通知

## Problem｜問題
顧客無法及時知道配送異常，
導致反覆查詢客服。

## Requirement｜需求
R-01：配送異常發生後，
系統應發送明確的異常通知。

狀態：需求候選，待業務確認。

## Hypothesis｜假設
H-01：主動通知異常及處理方式，
可以降低顧客重複查詢。

狀態：尚未驗證。

## Metric｜成功指標
M-01：通知成功送達率
公式：成功送達數 / 應通知事件數

M-02：重複查詢率
公式：指定期間內重複查詢的異常訂單數
      / 同期間符合條件的異常訂單數

M-03：異常處理完成時間
起點：異常首次被記錄
終點：異常處理完成且狀態確認

上述指標均需確認適用範圍、
資料來源、測量期間與成功門檻。

## Evidence｜證據
基準值：未測量
新系統結果：未測量
測試紀錄：尚未取得

## Change Log｜變更紀錄
C-01：待確認是否新增通知重試機制
原因：通知可能無法成功送達
決策者：待確認
日期：待確認
狀態：提案中

paragraphs: The template describes customers repeatedly contacting support because they do not learn about delivery exceptions promptly. R-01 proposes clear notifications after an exception, with business confirmation still pending. H-01 proposes that proactive notices and handling instructions can reduce repeated inquiries; it remains unverified. M-01 divides delivered notifications by events requiring a notice. M-02 divides exception orders with repeated inquiries during a defined period by all eligible exception orders in that period. M-03 measures from the first exception record to confirmed resolution. Scope, data sources, measurement periods and success thresholds still need confirmation. The baseline, new-system result and test records remain unmeasured or unavailable. C-01 proposes notification retries because delivery may fail; the decision maker and date remain unconfirmed and the change remains a proposal. The document has two practical benefits.
First, it connects the problem, requirement, hypothesis, metrics and evidence rather than recording only a feature list.
Second, it distinguishes intended results from results already demonstrated.
An AI-generated test plan does not justify marking a test as passed.
AI can help write requirements, design test cases and organize execution records. It should not claim acceptance is complete when the actual results have not been observed.

sections.heading: 9. Turn the lesson into an executable work method
paragraphs: When designing your next AI system, whether for healthcare, education, research or business, start with these five tasks.

blocks.caption: Table 6
rows: What exactly are we trying to improve?
Why do we believe this design helps?
Metrics, denominators, baseline, thresholds and data sources
How will we handle testing and changes?
Test evidence, acceptance decisions and change records

paragraphs: This approach follows the sequence in the GOV.UK service performance guidance: understand service purpose, develop hypotheses, decide what to measure, find data sources, and revise based on results. The source is listed below this lesson.
For formal acceptance, define pass conditions for important metrics in advance and consider sample representativeness, risk, cost and measurement uncertainty.

sections.heading: 10. Check your understanding: can you identify unsupported success claims?
paragraphs: Use the following synthetic case to examine claims and evidence.

blocks.caption: Figure 6 | Integrated case: AI quality inspection in manufacturing
blocks.description: All numbers are hypothetical. The study arrangement, sample representativeness and timing boundaries have not been provided.

items.title: The company makes three claims
items.body:
“AI has been successfully launched.”

“Defect detection performs well.”

“Overall factory production efficiency has improved by 30%.”

items.title: Genuinely defective products
items.body: 20 products

items.title: Defective products successfully blocked
items.body: 18 products

items.title: Genuinely good products
items.body: 80 products

items.title: Good products incorrectly blocked
items.body: 12 products

items.title: Previous manual workflow
items.body: Average 10 minutes

items.title: New AI workflow
items.body: Average 7 minutes

paragraphs: Answer the following questions:

1. Metric calculation: what are the defect blocking rate and the correct release rate for good products? What does each tell us?
2. Evidence judgment: does a change from 10 minutes to 7 minutes establish a 30% improvement in production efficiency? What information is missing?
3. Hypothesis testing: how would you make “AI can reduce quality-inspection costs” into a testable hypothesis?
4. Requirements traceability: if recalibrating the machine may invalidate previous pass decisions, what requirement and records would you add?
5. Overall decision: as project lead, would you roll out fully, continue a limited trial, or stop the project? Why?
Try answering first, then expand the reference explanations to check your reasoning and calculations.
Good engineering makes the rationale, success criteria and supporting evidence for decisions clear.

exercise.environment: problem.md, a text editor and this lesson’s synthetic arithmetic. Do not collect actual participant scores or timing.
steps: Choose one functional and one task metric. Define denominators, start/end conditions, sources and unmeasured fields.
Calculate the synthetic result with four missing-input cases and three blocked exports. Explain why complete inputs are excluded and handle a zero denominator separately.
Add H-01, R-01 and one change with sources, confirming role and reason. Ask a peer to identify the next claim needing verification.
exercise.expected: Reproducible metric definitions, assumptions, proposed requirements and change records in problem.md, with results honestly left unmeasured.
exercise.check: Calculate 3/4 = 75% and identify failure to meet this version’s blocking requirement. Do not treat synthetic arithmetic as actual participant or software results.
exercise.cleanup: Retain synthetic labels and original definitions. Do not publish actual participant task records. Keep unmeasured items unmeasured.

openChecks.prompt: Metric calculation: what are the defect blocking rate and the correct release rate for good products? What does each tell us?
answer: The defect blocking rate is 18/20 = 90%. The correct release rate for good products is (80−12)/80 = 85%. The first addresses missed defects; the second addresses false blocks. Neither alone establishes good overall performance.

openChecks.prompt: Evidence judgment: does a change from 10 minutes to 7 minutes establish a 30% improvement in production efficiency? What information is missing?
answer: The illustrative task time falls by 30%, from 10 to 7 minutes. This does not establish a 30% improvement in overall factory production efficiency. Fix tasks, difficulty, timing boundaries, output quality and checking/correction time; record failures, abandonment, samples and other variables. Output per fixed work period and time per item also have different percentage changes. Factory-level effects cannot be inferred from these data.

openChecks.prompt: Hypothesis testing: how would you make “AI can reduce quality-inspection costs” into a testable hypothesis?
answer: For example: within predefined products and a measurement period, AI-assisted inspection reduces total inspection cost per acceptable output while missed defects and false blocks remain within agreed guardrails. Define the baseline, cost boundary, comparison, sample and threshold; include equipment, human review, rework and error costs. No cost reduction or worse quality guardrails would leave the hypothesis unsupported.

openChecks.prompt: Requirements traceability: if recalibrating the machine may invalidate previous pass decisions, what requirement and records would you add?
answer: Require recalibration to invalidate affected previous pass results, with a new check before release. Record calibration version, affected data scope, R/H/M/T/C/E links, source, confirming role, date, rationale and status. Mark evidence pending until tests run; then attach actual evidence and decisions.

openChecks.prompt: Overall decision: as project lead, would you roll out fully, continue a limited trial, or stop the project? Why?
answer: The current information does not support full rollout. A limited trial is reasonable only with controllable risk, clear guardrails, stopping conditions and an evidence plan. Stop or defer if risk or cost cannot be controlled. State the rationale, missing evidence and next decision gate; synthetic records do not establish that a real trial has occurred.
